Rule.name: Fixed International Mother Language Day
Rule.comment: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1999 (resolution 30C/29) and first observed on 21 February 2000, to promote linguistic and cultural diversity. The date marks the 1952 shooting of students protesting for recognition of the Bengali language in Dhaka.

Rule.name: Fixed World Poetry Day
Rule.comment: Proclaimed by UNESCO at its 30th General Conference in Paris in 1999, to support linguistic expression through poetic form and to promote the reading, writing, and teaching of poetry worldwide.

Rule.name: Fixed World Theatre Day
Rule.comment: Established in 1961 by the International Theatre Institute (ITI) and first celebrated on 27 March 1962. The date was chosen following a proposal by Finnish diplomat Arvi Kivimaa at the ITI World Congress in Vienna.

Rule.name: Fixed International Jazz Day
Rule.comment: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2011 (resolution 36C/38) and first celebrated on 30 April 2012. Championed by jazz musician and UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador Herbie Hancock.

Rule.name: Fixed World Music Day
Rule.comment: Fête de la Musique. Originated in France in 1982 following a proposal by the French Ministry of Culture; now celebrated internationally on the summer solstice, 21 June, with free public performances.

Rule.name: Fixed International Friendship Day
Rule.comment: Proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 2011 (resolution 65/275). The concept originated in 1958 when the World Friendship Crusade proposed 30 July as World Friendship Day.

Rule.name: Fixed Star Wars Day
Rule.comment: An informal international fan observance of the Star Wars franchise, held on 4 May because of the phrase 'May the Fourth be with you'.
